title: Lotus Blossom
summary: Lotus Blossom, tracked elsewhere as Spring Dragon and RADIUM, is a China-nexus espionage cluster active since at least 2012, targeting government, diplomatic, military-adjacent and technology organisations, with a strong focus on Southeast Asia. Reporting describes exploiting internet-facing servers and network devices, including routers, for initial access and command and control, which lets operators hide activity inside traffic administrators treat as infrastructure noise. The group is also associated with delivering malware through weaponised documents and using living-off-the-land binaries to reduce its footprint. Attribution to Chinese state interests is an analytic judgement to present with uncertainty, and documented tool families come from vendor research rather than official statements.

beginner.definition: Lotus Blossom, also called Spring Dragon, is a spying group that public reports link to Chinese state interests. It targets government, diplomatic and technology organisations, especially in Southeast Asia. It often uses network devices such as routers as a hiding place. Researchers track it under several other names as well.
beginner.whyItMatters: Many teams watch laptops and servers but forget the network equipment in between. If an intruder controls a router, they can watch traffic, redirect it and stay hidden. That equipment often runs old software and keeps few records. So a quiet compromise there can last for years. Covering these devices closes a gap that attackers clearly know about.
howItWorks: The attackers look for network devices and servers that still use default settings or old software.
They take control of that device and use it as a base for watching and redirecting network traffic.
From there they reach internal systems and look for accounts with broader permissions.
They send documents that look official, and opening them starts hidden software on a computer.
They prefer tools already present in the system, so few new files appear on the disk.
They collect interesting documents and move them out through the compromised device.
beginner.example: Imagine a post office where a clerk quietly swaps the address labels on selected parcels. The parcels still arrive, so nobody complains and nothing looks broken. The clerk reads every letter that passes his desk and keeps copies for himself. Network equipment can be misused in exactly this way, which is why it needs watching too.
takeaways: Routers and other network devices need updates, strong passwords and logging, just like servers.
Software that is already installed on a system can be turned against you, so unusual use matters.
Official-looking documents remain one of the most common ways to start an intrusion.

objectives: Describe Lotus Blossom and the sectors and regions its campaigns are reported to target.
Explain why network infrastructure devices are attractive to an espionage operator.
Describe how traffic redirection from a compromised device can hide other activity.
Explain the defensive value of logging and firmware patching on edge devices.
Identify the signs that a network device has been modified without a change record.
State the limits of public attribution for this group without overstating confidence.
